What I Built Golden Hour is a calm, mobile-first web app that nudges you to step outside around sunrise and sunset. You pick sunrise, sunset or both, and how many minutes ahead you want a reminder. When it's time, your phone gets a notification such as "Golden hour in 20 minutes. Take your chai out to the terrace." general.title: 🌿 Terra-Gotchi: The 100% Offline AI Companion That Feeds on Real-World Nature
general.describe: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built Wellness apps usually trap you in a new cycle of screen time. I wanted to build something that forces you to use your phone simply as a viewfinder for the physical world 🏞️. Meet Terra-Gotchi 🐾—an open-source, fully offline digital pet that survives strictly by "eating" real-world natural textures 🍂. general.title: 5 ways Cancel doesn't actually cancel in C#
general.describe: A user clicks Export , changes their mind, and clicks Cancel . The spinner goes away. On the server, the export keeps running to the end and saves a file nobody wants. CancellationToken only works if every piece of code along the way cooperates. Here are five ways it quietly doesn't. Each demo logs a timestamp, the "Cancel" click is simulated, and every output is copied from actually running it on .NET 10. general.title: JSON Tiles: Fast Analytics on Semi-Structured Data (2021)
general.describe: Abstract: Developers often prefer flexibility over upfront schema design, making semi-structured data formats such as JSON increasingly popular. Large amounts of JSON data are therefore stored and analyzed by relational database systems. In existing systems, however, JSON’s lack of a fixed schema results in slow analytics. In this paper, we present JSON tiles, which, without losing the flexibility of JSON, enables relational systems to perform analytics on JSON data at native speed.
